forecast.author: MIST
forecast.method: Anchored on the unit-normalized consensus (ESPN, Sleeper, CBS, FantasyPros; FFToday failed in this pack) and the tiered historical actual/projection quantiles (starter tier median 0.82x to 0.88x, q25-q75 about 0.56x to 1.3x), then moved each line by hand for role (volume feed: snaps, targets, carries; volume sticky, touchdowns noise), the Vegas line and implied total, weather and injury status. Method rules applied: a personal ratio at three or more weeks on sticky volume blends into the median (Walker, McBride); a role read needs two weeks that actually point the same way (the week 5 Watson lesson); a sub-50%-snap committee or receiving back gets a 90% floor of 0 (Harvey). Bye and DOUBTFUL bench players carry zero lines. The pending Shrader claim is not on the roster and is not here.

players.name: Kenneth Walker III
players.why: Consensus 21.8 and all four sources inside 1.8 of each other. Kansas City -8.5 vs the Chargers, implied 25.5, a favorite's script for a back on 28.9 opportunities a game. Four weeks at about 1.5x of projection (34.1, 23.8, 21.3, 30.9) on sticky volume, so the method rule blends his own ratio with the elite-tier 0.88x: 19 from the tier, 32 from his ratio, 23 as the blend. The feed's ROLE-DOWN mark is a one-week dip in target share, not snaps (75%), so it does not move the median.

review_note:
**Coverage.** 10 of 14 lines inside the 50 (0.71) and 13 of 14 inside the 90 (0.93), MAE 5.41; the baseline 0.43, 0.93 and 5.81. Win probability 0.80 for a 96.1 to 89.5 win (Brier 0.04, baseline 0.043). Season to date (81 lines): 50% coverage 0.53, 90% 0.93, MAE 6.89 against the baseline's 0.46, 0.85 and 7.23. Alarm 1 (0.50 +/- 0.14 at 81 lines, so 0.36 to 0.64): not tripped. Alarm 2 (a middle slice at 35% or more, first checked this week): the q75-q95 slice sits at 34%, one point under the line, with 4%, 16%, 24%, 20%, 34%, 3% across the six slices; results land above the median more often than below, so the tier medians (0.82x to 0.94x on the consensus) may be a little low for starters. Watched, not acted on: the alarm did not trip and no reason failed. Weighted interval score on the same 71 lines: MIST 3.01, baseline 3.15 (-0.14, standard error 0.10); win log score MIST 0.572, baseline 0.632 over five weeks. Source MAE, best first: ESPN 5.02 (n 55), MIST 5.03 (n 71), consensus 5.11, Sleeper 6.07, CBS 6.10, FantasyPros 6.55 (n 17). Closing line value on 56 lines: MIST's leans correlate 0.144 with the market's later move but agree in sign on only 12 of 28 moves (0.43), against 0.50 for the consensus and ESPN; MIST's MAE against the market's later number is 5.89, the consensus 5.69, ESPN 5.58, the closing market 5.54. The hand moves still do not pay, so the probation rule stands and the week 7 forecast starts every median at the consensus times the tier median. FantasyPros judge: no week 6 row, because the Mac slept through both Sunday runs and the snapshot was never taken (the 10-18 7:06 PM routine-log line); the running mean stays at the 31-week backtest (+0.126 a scored player-week for MIST) with no live week yet.

**Misses, judged.** (1) Rhamondre Stevenson 3.6 against 11 to 21 (90: 5 to 31), the one line outside the 90, and a reasoning error, not variance: the median was lifted from the tier's 14.5 to 16 on "Henderson expected to miss multiple weeks" (Schefter, Monday), and Henderson played (7 carries, 31 yards). Stevenson had the 60% snaps and 14 carries the line assumed but 0 targets and 36 yards; the role did not vacate. The floor of 5 also sat at the tier q05 (0.34x of 16.5), so even the unmoved line had the result in its tail. Lesson, written as a one-case rule under *Weekly forecast and review*: a teammate's reported absence moves a median only when the injury report says OUT, IR or DOUBTFUL; a news line that a player is "expected to miss" is priced at the measured questionable rate (0.45 to 0.73), not as a vacated role. (2) RJ Harvey 14.6 against 3 to 10 (in the 90): a touchdown on 6 carries and 4 targets at 40% snaps; the band's shape was right for a receiving back and the top of the 90 (19) held it. Variance, no change. (3) Our total 96.1 against 105 to 134 (in the 90): Stevenson, the Rams D/ST 2.0 on a 7 median against a 19.5 implied opponent, and Christian Watson 9.4 on 8 targets; three low draws in a well-shaped week. No change. The opponent's total (89.5 against 80 to 108) and the standing (#1, inside the 50) landed.
